summary: Socket affinity fanout causing regional GPU islanding and autoscale blind-spot
description:
Issue summary: Over the 11:40–13:20 UTC window on 2026-03-12 NimbusSearch observed sustained p50/p95 throughput loss in their dedicated pool while aggregate cluster-level metrics looked nominal. Impact: customer production traffic experienced 20–40% reduction in successful inferences per GPU and elevated p99 latencies (3x). Observed failures were primarily timeouts and 429-like throttles from the dedicated pool facade.

Environment: dedicated pool hosted in us-east (tenant: nimbus-prod, reserved capacity).

Timeline / key events: 
- 2026-03-12 11:38 UTC: Customer reports increased application-side queue lengths to Support.
- 2026-03-12 11:45 UTC: Support escalates to SRE after brief check; core metrics (GPU count, cluster CPU) appear within usual ranges.
- 2026-03-12 12:05 UTC: Observability shows handful of GPUs at sustained 95–100% utilization while the rest underutilized. Autoscaler did not trigger new allocations for ~25 minutes.
- 2026-03-12 12:20 UTC: SRE notices a connection fanout pattern from a small set of customer session IPs -> affinity mapped to GPUs 8–11, leaving others idle (GPU islanding).

Steps to reproduce (internal / best-effort):
1) Replay a production traffic trace that preserves client connection affinity (keepalives + pinned sockets) into a dedicated pool with identical scheduler affinity config.
2) Simulate long-lived multiplexed short streams from a single client ID (10k concurrent sockets with low per-req tokens).
3) Observe allocation and batcher placement; look for persistent slot reservations on NVLink islanded GPUs and autoscaler non-reactivity.

Observed behavior: 
- Asymmetric connection distribution caused repeated placement on a small GPU subset.
- Batching engine experienced slot serialization (many tiny batches) on those GPUs, increasing per-token overhead.
- Autoscaler metrics (aggregate free_slots / average_utilization) were masked because the majority of GPUs were underutilized; autoscaler thresholds were not met.

Expected behavior: 
- The scheduler should spread short-stream fanout across GPUs and the autoscaler should be sensitive to per-GPU skew (not only cluster aggregate).

Logs & dashboards (pointers): 
- Grafana: /d/redwood/dedicated-pool-tenant?var-tenant=nimbus-prod&from=167/ -- panel "per-gpu-utilization" shows skew.
- Kibana traces: trace ids included in comments.
- Customer-provided app logs attached to ticket.
comments: 2026-03-12 11:51 - Support (Aisha Patel): Received initial report from NimbusSearch. Customer reports timeouts and increased tail latencies. Asked for application logs and sample request IDs.

2026-03-12 12:10 - SRE (Marco Nguyen): Quick triage shows per-GPU skew; opening deeper investigation. Noting GPUs 8-11 pinned at high utilization while others idle. Suspect socket affinity/scheduler placement interaction.

2026-03-12 12:28 - Customer (Elena Morales, NimbusSearch): We pushed a short-stream optimization in our SDK last night that uses persistent multiplexed connections. Happy to provide trace captures. We do see lots of very short requests (avg 8 tokens) from a few hosts.

2026-03-12 12:40 - Runtime Eng (Priya Singh): Ran replay with similar short-stream fanout. Reproduced slot serialization on GPUs mapped to the same NUMA/NVLink island. Autoscaler didn't add nodes — cluster-level free_slots metric remained above threshold because many GPUs were idle.

2026-03-12 12:55 - SRE (Marco Nguyen): Temporary mitigation applied: forced soft-eviction of affinity cache for affected tenancy and applied per-gpu-skew alert to trigger immediate autoscale override. Asking customer to throttle persistent connections while we prepare a targeted fix.

2026-03-13 09:10 - Customer (Elena Morales): After the mitigation, throughput recovered to baseline. We plan to ship an SDK patch to round-robin new connections by default; coordinating timing with Redwood.
2026-03-13 11:00 - Support (Aisha Patel): Noted recovery. Scheduling longer postmortem and follow-up implementation items for scheduler changes to avoid future islanding.
investigation_notes: Affinity analysis: Scheduler uses source-ip hash + port to prefer stable placement. Combination of persistent multiplexed sockets and small request sizes favored repeated reuse of same batcher slots.
Autoscaler blind-spot: global_utilization based autoscale rule masked per-GPU hot spots. Add per_gpu_skew_ratio metric to detect imbalance.
Batcher behavior: tiny-batch overhead dominates when many short requests hit same GPU; continuous batching window rarely filled, producing many micro-batches.
NVLink/NUMA mapping: GPUs 8-11 share NVLink island, scheduler affinity prioritized placement there due to historical locality preference which in this case amplified the problem.
Customer SDK change: persistent connection reuse + high concurrency produced concentrated fanout. Customer will patch to more balanced socket distribution.
Reproduction: Successful in internal staging when reproducing same connection-fanout characteristics; validated mitigation (evict affinity cache) resolves skew temporarily.
resolution_summary:
Mitigation applied: evicted affinity cache for tenant nimbus-prod and enabled emergency per-gpu-skew override which forced autoscaler to provision 2 extra GPUs in us-east. Customer throttled new persistent connections briefly and rolled back SDK change. Result: throughput returned to baseline and p99 dropped to normal levels.

Permanent fix plan: scheduler change to include bounded placement randomness for highly multiplexed short-streams; autoscaler enhancement to consider per_gpu_skew_ratio and trigger earlier. Both items scheduled on SRE roadmap.

Rollout notes: we will deploy a scheduler tweak (canary) to staging on 2026-03-18 and to prod on 2026-03-20 behind a tenant toggle. Autoscaler metric addition targeted for 2026-03-25.
follow_up_actions: Create a per-gpu skew alert: SRE ticket INT-9876 (owner: Marco Nguyen)
Scheduler change PR: runtime#4128 (owner: Priya Singh) — add bounded randomness when request length < 16 tokens and connection count > 1024
Autoscaler change PR: autoscaler#221 (owner: Ravi Patel) — include per-gpu_skew_ratio and override policy
Customer SDK guidance: update NimbusSearch SDK recommendations to avoid single-host socket fanout; doc snippet to be added to support KB
